# iliad-153 — new renderings (24.93–199)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἄριστον (ἐντύνοντο ἄριστον, 24.124) | "made ready breakfast" | "preparing breakfast" | "the morning meal"; follows the table's ἄριστον "breakfast" (16.2) |
| ὄϊς λάσιος μέγας ἱέρευτο (24.125) | "a woolly, great sheep … had been slaughtered" | "a great woolly sheep had been slaughtered" | "shaggy", "sacrificed"; ἱερεύω keeps "slaughter" (23.147) |
| ἐπένοντο (24.123–124) | "busied themselves" | "busied themselves" | "toiled at", "were busy"; keeps the table's πένομαι "busy oneself" |
| ὀδυρόμενος καὶ ἀχεύων (24.128) | "grieving and sorrowing" | "grieving and sorrowing" | "lamenting", "mourning"; ὀδύρομαι keeps "grieve" (22.424); ἀχεύω "sorrow" (its 5.869 row has only "grieving in heart") |
| σὴν ἔδεαι κραδίην (24.129) | "are you eating your heart" | "will you go on eating your heart" | "devouring", "consuming"; figure kept literal |
| μεμνημένος οὔτέ τι σίτου οὔτ’ εὐνῆς (24.129–130) | "mindful of neither any food nor bed" | "with no thought for food or for bed" | "remembering neither …" (reads as forgetting); the negatives belong to the participle |
| ἀγαθὸν δὲ γυναικί περ ἐν φιλότητι μίσγεσθ’ (24.130–131) | "good it is, even with a woman, in love to mingle" | "it is good to lie in love even with a woman" | "to make love"; μίσγομαι ἐν φιλότητι is "mingle" in `l` and "lie … in love" in `i` (2.232); changed at review from "mingle" in `i` |
| οὐ γάρ μοι δηρὸν βέῃ (24.131) | "for not for long will you live, for me" | "for you will not live long, as far as I am concerned" | "to me you will not live long"; βέῃ is a future "you will live", μοι the dative of the person concerned |
| ἄγχι παρέστηκεν θάνατος καὶ μοῖρα κραταιή (24.132) | "near has taken its stand death and strong fate" | "death and strong fate stand close beside you" | "mighty fate"; keeps the table's μοῖρα κραταιή "strong fate" |
| Διὸς δέ τοι ἄγγελός εἰμι (24.133, 24.173) | "and of Zeus, to you, a messenger I am" (24.133, 24.173) | "I am a messenger of Zeus to you" | "Zeus's herald"; ἄγγελος keeps "messenger"; the same English at 133 and 173 |
| κεχολῶσθαι (24.114, 24.135) | "am angered" / "is angered" | "am angry at him" / "is angry at you" | "enraged" (kept for the speech-introduction χολωσαμένη, 3.413); χολόω keeps "angered" / "angry" (6.205, 16.320, 24.65); changed at review from "enraged" |
| σκύζεσθαι (24.113, 24.134) | "are sullen at" | "are sullen toward" | "are angry" ("angry" is reserved for χόλος in the Iliad rows), "are incensed" (χώομαι); follows the Iliad rows σκυζομένη "sullen" (4.23, 8.483, 9.198); the Odyssey row 23.213 "be angry" is not followed; changed at review |
| ἔξοχα πάντων ἀθανάτων (24.113–114, 24.134–135) | "above all of the immortals" | "above all the immortals" | "outstandingly", "most of all"; ἔξοχα keeps "above all others" (5.61) |
| φρεσὶ μαινομένῃσιν (24.114, 24.135) | "with raging wits" | "in his / your raging wits" | "frenzied", "mad"; μαίνομαι keeps "rage" (5.185), φρένες "wits" |
| Ἕκτορ’ ἔχει παρὰ νηυσὶ κορωνίσιν οὐδ’ ἀπέλυσεν (24.115, 24.136) | "he holds by the curved ships and did not release him" | "keeps Hector by the curved ships and has not released him" | "gave back", "ransomed" (λύσασθαι is the middle, "ransom"); ἀπολύω keeps "release" (10.449); κορωνίς "curved" (19.182) |
| αἴ κέν πως ἐμέ τε δείσῃ ἀπό θ’ Ἕκτορα λύσῃ (24.116) | "in case perhaps he may fear me and release Hector" | "in case he somehow fears me and releases Hector" | "if he fears me and gives Hector back"; αἴ κε keeps "if / in case" (9.172), the tmesis ἀπό … λύσῃ is one verb |
| αἰδῶ καὶ φιλότητα τεήν (24.111) | "your regard and love" | "my regard and love for you" | "shame" (the table's αἰδώς), "respect", "reverence"; a departure from "shame": here αἰδώς is regard for a person, not shame; kept at review (the table's αἰδέομαι "respect", 4.402, shows the stem allows it); the note now also says the possessor is open |
| τόδε κῦδος Ἀχιλλῆϊ προτιάπτω (24.110) | "this glory to Achilles attach" | "I am giving Achilles this glory" | "fasten on", "lay upon"; κῦδος "glory" (5.33); προσάπτω is "fasten on", `i` by sense |
| ἐπίτειλον (24.112) | "lay a charge" | "give … this charge" | "command", "bid"; keeps the table's ἐπιτέλλω "charge" (2.10) |
| τά κε θυμὸν ἰήνῃ (24.119 = 147 = 176 = 196) | "which may warm his heart" | "that will cheer his heart" | "soothe" (the table turns it down for ἰάνθη, 23.598), "gladden", "melt"; ἰαίνω is "warm" in `l` (root sense), "cheer" in `i` as in the table; changed at review from "soothe" |
| ὃς ἄποινα φέροι καὶ νεκρὸν ἄγοιτο (24.139) | "let him who brings ransom also take away the corpse" | "let him who brings ransom take the corpse away" | "carries off", "take back"; ἄγοιτο is a middle optative, "for himself" |
| τῇδ’ εἴη (24.139) | "Thus let it be" | "So be it" | "Let it be so"; the optative of wish |
| θυμῷ πρόφρονι (24.140) | "with a ready-minded heart" | "with a ready heart" | "willing", "gladly"; follows the table's πρόφρων "ready-minded" (8.39) |
| ἐν νηῶν ἀγύρει (24.141) | "in the gathering of the ships" | "in the throng of the ships" | "in the assembly of the ships", "among the ships"; ἀγύρις "gathering" in `l`, "throng" in `i` (16.661); changed at review |
| ἔπεα πτερόεντ’ ἀγόρευον (24.142, plural subject) | "many winged words … spoke" | "spoke many winged words" | "addressed"; follows the table's 3.155 row |
| Ἶριν δ’ ὄτρυνε Κρονίδης εἰς Ἴλιον ἱρήν (24.143, whole line) | "And Iris the son-of-Cronus urged on to sacred Ilium:" | "And the son of Cronus urged Iris on to sacred Ilium:" | "sent", "roused"; ὀτρύνω keeps "urge on" (4.73); Κρονίδης "son of Cronus"; Ἴλιον ἱρήν "sacred Ilium" (7.413) |
| βάσκ’ ἴθι Ἶρι ταχεῖα λιποῦσ’ ἕδος Οὐλύμποιο (24.144, speech opening) | "Go, set out, swift Iris, having left the seat of Olympus" | "Be off with you, swift Iris, leaving the seat of Olympus" | "hasten"; follows the table's 11.186 row (βάσκ’ ἴθι Ἶρι ταχεῖα) and ἕδος "seat" (5.367) |
| ἄγγειλον (24.145) | "announce" | "bring word" | "report", "tell"; aorist imperative of ἀγγέλλω |
| κῆρύξ τίς οἱ / τοι ἕποιτο γεραίτερος, ὅς κ’ ἰθύνοι ἡμιόνους καὶ ἄμαξαν ἐΰτροχον (24.149–150 = 178–179) | "Let some herald, an older man, follow him / you, who may guide straight the mules and the well-rolling wagon" | "Let some older herald follow him / you, to guide the mules and the well-rolling wagon straight" | "steer", "drive" (avoided in the table's ἰθύνει row); κῆρυξ "herald"; ἄμαξα ἐύτροχος "well-rolling wagon" (6.72) |
| ἠδὲ καὶ αὖτις νεκρὸν ἄγοι προτὶ ἄστυ (24.150–151 = 179–180) | "and also back again might lead the corpse toward the town" | "and who is also to bring the corpse back toward the town" | "city" (ἄστυ keeps "town", 2.801) |
| μὴ δέ τί οἱ θάνατος μελέτω φρεσὶ μὴ δέ τι τάρβος (24.152 = 181) | "And let not death at all be a care to him in his wits, nor any fear" | "Let death be no care to him in his wits, nor any fear" | "concern", "dread"; τάρβος "fear" (ταρβέω "be afraid", 21.288) |
| τοῖον πομπὸν ὀπάσσομεν ἀργεϊφόντην (24.153) | "such an escort we shall give him, Argeïphontes" | "we shall give him such an escort, the slayer of Argus" | "guide" (kept for διάκτορος, 2.103), "conductor"; πομπός "escort"; ἀργεϊφόντης keeps the table's row (disputed meaning) |
| εἷός κεν ἄγων Ἀχιλῆϊ πελάσσῃ (24.154 = 183) | "until, leading, he brings … near to Achilles" | "until, leading …, he brings … close to Achilles" | "till", "while"; εἷος "until" (17.730); πελάζω "bring near" (13.180) |
| ἐπὴν ἀγάγῃσιν … οὔτ’ αὐτὸς κτενέει ἀπό τ’ ἄλλους πάντας ἐρύξει (24.155–156 = 184–185) | "neither will he himself kill, and all the others he will hold back" | "Achilles will not kill him himself, and he will hold back all the others" | "keep off", "ward off"; ἐρύκω "hold back" (13.751); `i` names Achilles because the subject changes from Hermes to Achilles |
| οὔτ’ ἄφρων οὔτ’ ἄσκοπος οὔτ’ ἀλιτήμων (24.157 = 186) | "neither senseless nor heedless nor an offender" | "neither senseless, nor heedless, nor a transgressor" | "foolish", "careless", "sinful"; ἄφρων "senseless" (17.586); ἄσκοπος and ἀλιτήμων are rare and the note says their sense is not certain |
| ἐνδυκέως ἱκέτεω πεφιδήσεται ἀνδρός (24.158 = 187) | "very kindly a suppliant man he will spare" | "will spare a man who comes as a suppliant, and spare him very kindly" | "carefully", "mercifully"; ἐνδυκέως keeps "kindly" (10.65); πεφιδήσεται "spare" with the genitive |
| ἀελλόπος Ἶρις ἀγγελέουσα (24.159) | published (iliad-050, 24.159) | published | the packet's English is taken whole |
| κίχεν δ’ ἐνοπήν τε γόον τε (24.160) | "found shouting and lament" | "found shouting and lament" | "wailing"; ἐνοπή "shouting" (12.35), γόος "lament" (10.409) |
| δάκρυσιν εἵματ’ ἔφυρον (24.162) | "were soaking their clothes with tears" | "soaking their clothes with tears" | "staining", "wetting"; φύρω "soak, drench"; εἵματα "clothes" (2.261) |
| παῖδες … θυγατέρες … νυοί (24.161, 166) | "sons" … "daughters" … "daughters-in-law" | "sons" … "daughters" … "daughters-in-law" | "children" (παῖδες is "sons" because it is set against θυγατέρες) |
| ἐντυπὰς ἐν χλαίνῃ κεκαλυμμένος (24.163) | "closely wrapped in his cloak, covered over" | "wrapped close in his cloak" | "huddled", "curled up"; ἐντυπάς is rare, the note says the sense is not certain |
| κόπρος … καταμήσατο (24.164–165) | "dung … he had scraped together" | "dung … he had scraped together" | "filth", "ashes"; κόπρος "dung" (17.297); καταμήσατο is rare, traditionally "scrape together", the note says its sense is not certain |
| ἀνὰ δώματ’ ὠδύροντο (24.166) | "were grieving" | "grieved throughout the house" | "wailed", "lamented"; ὀδύρομαι "grieve" (22.424) |
| χερσὶν ὑπ’ Ἀργείων κέατο ψυχὰς ὀλέσαντες (24.168) | published (iliad-085, 24.168 line) | published | the published line is kept |
| τυτθὸν φθεγξαμένη (24.170) | "uttering a little" | "in a low voice" | "softly", "faintly"; τυτθόν "a little" (22.494), the note gives the sense |
| τὸν δὲ τρόμος ἔλλαβε γυῖα (24.170) | "him trembling seized, the limbs" | "a trembling took hold of his limbs" | "shuddering", "shaking"; follows the table's τρόμος εἷλεν (5.862) and γυῖα "limbs" |
| θάρσει Δαρδανίδη Πρίαμε φρεσί (24.171) | "Take courage, Dardanus’ descendant Priam, in your wits" | "Take courage in your wits, Priam, descendant of Dardanus" | "son of Dardanus"; follows θάρσει "Take courage" (4.184) and Δαρδανίδης "descendant of Dardanus" (3.303) |
| κακὸν ὀσσομένη τόδ’ ἱκάνω (24.172) | "foreboding evil, am I coming here" | "I do not come here foreboding evil" | "with evil intent"; keeps the table's ὀσσόμενος "foreboding" (1.105), feminine |
| ἀλλ’ ἀγαθὰ φρονέουσα (24.173) | "but with good thoughts" | "but with good thoughts" | "with good will", "kindly"; φρονέω "think" |
| ὅς σευ ἄνευθεν ἐὼν μέγα κήδεται ἠδ’ ἐλεαίρει (24.174) | "who, though far from you, greatly cares for and pities you" | "who, though he is far from you, cares greatly for you and pities you" | "grieves for", "has compassion"; κήδομαι "care for" (1.196), ἐλεαίρω "pity" (2.27) |
| λύσασθαί σ’ ἐκέλευσεν Ὀλύμπιος Ἕκτορα δῖον (24.175) | "To ransom you bade, the Olympian, heavenly Hector" | "The Olympian has ordered you to ransom heavenly Hector" | "told", "bidden"; κελεύω "bid" in `l`, "order" in `i` (4.359, 5.528); Ὀλύμπιος "the Olympian" (2.309); δῖος "heavenly" |
| οἶον (24.147, 177) | "alone" | "himself alone" / "yourself alone" | "only"; accusative agreeing with the unspoken Priam |
| ἣ μὲν ἄρ’ ὣς εἰποῦσ’ ἀπέβη πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις (24.188) | published (iliad-050, 24.188 line) | published | the published first line is kept |
| ἄμαξαν ἐΰτροχον ἡμιονείην ὁπλίσαι ἠνώγει (24.189–190) | "the well-rolling, mule-drawn wagon to make ready bade" | "bade his sons make ready the well-rolling, mule-drawn wagon" | "told" (turned down for ἄνωγα, 7.386), "harness", "fit out"; ἄμαξα ἐύτροχος ἡμιονείη (6.72), ὁπλίζω "make ready" (7.417), ἄνωγα "bid" |
| πείρινθα δῆσαι ἐπ’ αὐτῆς (24.190) | "a basket to bind upon it" | "to bind a basket on it" | "wicker body", "box", "frame"; πείρινς is rare and the note says its sense is not certain |
| αὐτὸς δ’ ἐς θάλαμον κατεβήσετο κηώεντα (24.191) | the odyssey-072 wording | the odyssey-072 wording | the published Odyssey line is kept, "He himself went down into the fragrant chamber" |
| κέδρινον ὑψόροφον, ὃς γλήνεα πολλὰ κεχάνδει (24.192) | "of cedar, high-roofed, which held many treasures" | "a chamber of cedar with a high roof, which held many treasures" | "glittering things", "jewels", "hoard"; ὑψόροφος "high-roofed" (5.42); γλήνεα is rare, the note says the sense is not certain; χανδάνω "hold" |
| ἐς … ἐκαλέσσατο (24.193, tmesis) | "in he called" | "called … in" | "summoned", "called to him"; ἐσκαλέω with the prefix split from the verb, καλέω "call" (3.161) |
| δαιμονίη (24.194) | "Strange woman" | "Strange woman" | follows the table's δαιμονίη (4.31, 19.71) |
| Διόθεν μοι Ὀλύμπιος ἄγγελος ἦλθε (24.194) | "from Zeus to me an Olympian messenger came" | "an Olympian messenger has come to me from Zeus" | "heavenly messenger"; Ὀλύμπιος "Olympian", ἄγγελος "messenger" |
| τί τοι φρεσὶν εἴδεται εἶναι (24.197) | "what seems to you in your wits to be so" | "what does it seem to you, in your wits, to be" | "what do you think"; εἴδεται "seems" (1.228) |
| αἰνῶς … μένος καὶ θυμὸς ἄνωγε (24.198) | "dreadfully … my might and heart bid me" | "my very own might and heart dreadfully bid me" | "terribly" (turned down for αἰνῶς at 3.158); μένος "might" (2.387), θυμός "heart", ἄνωγα "bid" |
| κεῖσ’ ἰέναι ἐπὶ νῆας ἔσω στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν (24.199) | "to go there to the ships, into the wide army of the Achaeans" | "to go there to the ships, into the wide army of the Achaeans" | "broad host"; εὐρὺν στρατόν "the wide army" (4.209) |
| ἀκτὴν ἐξαναβᾶσαι (24.97) | "having climbed up out onto the headland" | "climbed up out of the sea onto the headland" | "shore"; ἀκτή keeps "headland" (2.395) |
| ἀϊχθήτην (24.97) | "darted" | "darted" | "rushed"; ἀΐσσω keeps "dart" (8.87) |
| εἶξε δ’ Ἀθήνη (24.100) | "gave way" | "gave way" | "made room", "yielded her seat"; εἴκω "give way" |
| ὤρεξε πιοῦσα (24.102) | "held it out" | "held the cup out" | "handed back", "gave back" (the Greek has no receiver) |
| ἐννῆμαρ δὴ νεῖκος ἐν ἀθανάτοισιν ὄρωρεν (24.107) | "For nine days now a quarrel … has arisen" | "For nine days now a quarrel has arisen" | "strife" (kept for ἔρις), "dispute"; ἐννῆμαρ "for nine days" (6.174), νεῖκος "quarrel", ὄρωρεν "has arisen" (11.500) |
| πτολιπόρθῳ (Ἀχιλλῆϊ πτολιπόρθῳ, 24.108) | "the city-sacking" | "sacker of cities" | "destroyer of cities"; follows the table's πτολίπορθος (2.728) |
| κλέψαι δ’ ὀτρύνουσιν ἐΰσκοπον ἀργεϊφόντην (24.109) | "and to steal him they urge the keen-sighted Argeïphontes" | "and they urge the keen-sighted slayer of Argus to steal him" | "rob", "carry off"; ἐΰσκοπος "keen-sighted" (7.137) |
| ἤλυθες Οὔλυμπον δὲ θεὰ Θέτι κηδομένη περ (24.104) | "You have come to Olympus, goddess Thetis, grieved though you are" | "You have come to Olympus, goddess Thetis, worried as you are" | "grieved" (the draft's first `i`), "though you care"; follows the 1.586 / 5.382 rows for κηδομένη περ ("grieved though you are" in `l`, "worried as you are" in `i`); changed at review |
| πένθος ἄλαστον ἔχουσα μετὰ φρεσίν (24.105) | "having an unforgettable grief in your wits" | "with a grief you cannot forget in your wits" | "unceasing", "unbearable"; follows the 24.423 row ἄλαστον πένθος "unforgettable grief", with the root uncertain (note) |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασα κάλυμμ’ ἕλε δῖα θεάων (24.93) | "So then, having spoken, she took a veil, heavenly-one of goddesses" | "With these words, heavenly even among goddesses, she took up a dark veil" | follows the table's ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασα … δῖα θεάων (18.388) and δῖα θεάων "heavenly even among goddesses" |
| κυάνεον … μελάντερον (24.94) | "dark … blacker" | "dark … blacker" | "blue"; κυάνεος "dark" (1.528) |
| ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε θεὰ Θέτις ἀργυρόπεζα (24.120, whole line) | "So he spoke, and did not disobey, the goddess Thetis, silver-footed," | "So Zeus spoke, and the goddess Thetis, silver-footed, did not disobey;" | "silver-heeled"; follows the 24.89 row (θεὰ Θέτις ἀργυρόπεζα) and the pattern of 2.166; the next line is the published 8.- line, kept |
| ἁδινὰ στενάχοντα (24.123) | "groaning heavily" | "groaning heavily" | table row, unchanged (23.225) |
| ἣ δὲ μάλ’ ἄγχ’ αὐτοῖο καθέζετο πότνια μήτηρ (24.126) | "And she very close beside him sat down, the lady mother" | "She sat down very close beside him, his lady mother" | "queenly mother"; πότνια μήτηρ "lady mother" (11.180) |
| τέκνον ἐμὸν (24.128) | "My child" | "my child" | "my son"; τέκνον "child" (1.362) |
| ἀλλ’ ἐμέθεν ξύνες ὦκα (24.133) | "give heed to me quickly" | "listen to me, and quickly" | follows the table's ξύνες ὦκα (2.26) |
| ἀλλ’ ἄγε δὴ λῦσον, νεκροῖο δὲ δέξαι ἄποινα (24.137) | "But come now, release him, and for the corpse accept ransom" | "So come now, release him, and accept ransom for the corpse" | "ransom him", "take the price"; ἄποινα "ransom" (1.13) |
| λύσασθαι φίλον υἱὸν ἰόντ’ ἐπὶ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν (24.118 = 146 = 195) | "to ransom his dear son, going to the ships of the Achaeans" | "to ransom his dear son, as he goes to the ships of the Achaeans" (195: "my … as I go") | "going to the ships" bare (reads as if the son goes); ἰόντ’ agrees with the unspoken Priam, as the note says; added at review |
